Web search: baseball swing phases mechanics sweet spot launch angle exit velocity
{"query": "baseball swing phases mechanics sweet spot launch angle exit velocity", "results": [{"tool_use_id": "srvtoolu_016Gn6VCLx85M762cpkTi19y", "content": [{"title": "Author Archive", "url": "https://community.fangraphs.com/author/drmarshall1/"}, {"title": "journal.unnes.ac.id", "url": "https://journal.unnes.ac.id/journals/jssf/article/download/17951/2932"}, {"title": "Reverse Engineering Swing Mechanics from Statcast Data", "url": "https://community.fangraphs.com/reverse-engineering-swing-mechanics-from-statcast-data/"}, {"title": "How A Batter Hits A Baseball: Physics Of A Home Run", "url": "https://grandavehousing.calpoly.edu/news/how-a-batter-hits-a"}, {"title": "The Influence of Swing Machines on Batted Ball Exit Velocity in MLB", "url": "https://sabr.org/?p=330183"}, {"title": "the science of hitting", "url": "https://sbrc2017.ufpa.br/trip/the-science-of-hitting"}, {"title": "The Influence of Swing Machines on Batted Ball Exit Velocity in MLB", "url": "https://sabr.org/journal/article/the-influence-of-swing-machines-on-batted-ball-exit-velocity-in-mlb/"}, {"title": "the science  of  hitting", "url": "https://feedback.uslawns.com/book-search/80g6dq/8FE158/the_science__of__hitting.pdf"}, {"title": "The Science Of Hitting A Baseball", "url": "https://curvymonthly.curvyyoga.com/fetch.php/Tzp4Hp/706756/The Science Of Hitting A Baseball.pdf"}]}, "The search results cover sweet spot, launch angle, and exit velocity, though little of it addresses swing phases directly.

**Sweet spot and energy transfer:** One source describes the sweet spot as the area where the bat transfers energy to the ball most efficiently, and says contact there minimizes vibration and maximizes exit velocity (The sweet spot on the bat is key. It's the area where the bat is most efficient at transferring energy to the ball. Hitting the ball on the sweet spot minimizes vibrations and maximizes the exit velocity of the ball.). A Fangraphs piece defines the sweet spot as a two-inch area centered six inches from the barrel, and reports that Blast Motion measures MLB bat speed there at 65 to 85 MPH (Measuring the speed of the bat at the sweet spot, a two-inch-long area whose center is located six inches from the barrel of the bat, Blast Motion reports that MLB players swing the bat between 65 and 85 MPH.).

**Launch angle:** Sources give different optimal ranges. One says a launch angle of around 20-30 degrees is generally optimal for hitting home runs, assuming the ball is hit with enough speed. Another gives a broader optimal launch angles typically range between 10 and 30 degrees, depending on the hitter's goal.

**Statcast barrel definition:** A Statcast barrel is a ball that has a combination of a launch angle between 26-30 degrees and an exit velocity of at least 98 mph, as cited in a Indonesian journal article.

**Mechanics and exit velocity:** A 2026 SABR study found that, with bat speed, height, and weight held constant, for attack direction and contact point, no significant correlation to exit velocity was found. The author suggests hitting performance is likely multifactorial, with swing path, kinetic sequencing, and bat speed playing more substantial roles than individual mechanical variables alone.

**Caveats:** I found no source that breaks the swing into phases (such as stance, load, stride, contact, and follow-through) or describes kinetic sequencing in detail. Several results are low-quality (anonymous PDFs and a generic study-guide style page), so the launch-angle ranges should be treated as approximate. The SABR study is the most rigorous source here, but its sample was small, and its authors call for more research."], "durationSeconds": 7.241498361000001, "searchCount": 1}

id: note:2:Web search: pitch types physics Magnus effect fast
name: Web search: pitch types physics Magnus effect fastball curveball slider changeup knuckleball screwball eephus
text:
Web search: pitch types physics Magnus effect fastball curveball slider changeup knuckleball screwball eephus
{"query": "pitch types physics Magnus effect fastball curveball slider changeup knuckleball screwball eephus", "results": [{"tool_use_id": "srvtoolu_01X2GcH8w9Zkr2PUWo4GXEfL", "content": [{"title": "The Physics of the different types of pitches in Baseball", "url": "https://prezi.com/5axib_af1bkk/the-physics-of-the-different-types-of-pitches-in-baseball"}, {"title": "The Physics Behind Baseball Pitches", "url": "https://www.comsol.com/blogs/physics-behind-baseball-pitches"}, {"title": "The Physics Behind Baseball Pitches", "url": "https://www.comsol.com/blogs/physics-behind-baseball-pitches?setlang=1"}, {"title": "The Physics of Baseball", "url": "https://artsci.washu.edu/node/2202"}, {"title": "comsol.com", "url": "https://comsol.com/blogs?p=34469"}, {"title": "the magnus effect why pitches move", "url": "https://texasleaguers.com/blog/2009/02/19/the-magnus-effect-why-pitches-move"}, {"title": "How to make a pitched ball curve to your will", "url": "https://www.snexplores.org/article/pitch-physics-curve-baseball-softball-cricket"}, {"title": "The Physics of Why Baseballs Do What They Do", "url": "https://tangotiger.net/files/sirkodiak.html"}, {"title": "Why Pitches Curve — The Magnus Effect", "url": "https://www.yagoonara.com/en/wiki/qna/magnus-effect"}]}, "The search turned up good physics coverage for most of the pitches, but nothing on the eephus and little on the changeup.

- **Magnus effect as the core mechanism:** Spin creates a pressure difference that pushes the ball sideways or up/down, depending on the spin axis. One source describes it as acting like an airplane wing, with backspin producing lift and topspin producing a downward force ([source](https://texasleaguers.com/blog/2009/02/19/the-magnus-effect-why-pitches-move)).
- **Fastball:** Backspin lifts the ball, so it drops less than gravity alone would make it drop, which gives it a "hidden" curve ([source](https://www.snexplores.org/article/pitch-physics-curve-baseball-softball-cricket)).
- **Curveball:** Heavy topspin adds a downward Magnus force on top of gravity. Curveballs typically drop roughly another 30 cm from this effect ([source](https://www.snexplores.org/article/pitch-physics-curve-baseball-softball-cricket)).
- **Slider:** Sidespin makes the ball move laterally ([source](https://artsci.washu.edu/node/2202)).
- **Screwball:** Spins similarly to a curveball but breaks in the opposite lateral direction for a given pitcher ([source](https://www.comsol.com/blogs/physics-behind-baseball-pitches)).
- **Knuckleball:** Pitchers aim for minimal spin. Without spin, the Magnus effect has almost no effect, and vortex shedding behind the ball causes small, unpredictable movement ([source](https://www.comsol.com/blogs/physics-behind-baseball-pitches)).
- **Changeup:** One source lists it among the common pitch categories and ranks its speed below the curveball, but offers no physics detail ([source](https://tangotiger.net/files/sirkodiak.html)).
- **Eephus:** Not covered in any of the results."], "durationSeconds": 7.0508322460000015, "searchCount": 1}

{"query": "baseball rules infield fly rule, walk-off, cycle, grand slam, rally cap, seventh-inning stretch", "results": [{"tool_use_id": "srvtoolu_01WrE6Ajua37s1PF2CxTLFt8", "content": [{"title": "Infield fly rule", "url": "https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Infield_fly_rule"}, {"title": "Baseball Walk-Off: Rules, Drama, & Unforgettable Wins", "url": "https://grandavehousing.calpoly.edu/news/baseball-walk-off-rules-drama"}, {"title": "Infield fly rule", "url": "https://www.Wikipedia.org/wiki/Infield_fly"}, {"title": "Decoding The Walk-Off Win: Baseball Rules Explained", "url": "https://grandavehousing.calpoly.edu/news/decoding-the-walk-off-win"}, {"title": "Infield fly rule", "url": "https://www.baseball-reference.com/bullpen/Infield_fly"}, {"title": "Infield fly rule", "url": "https://aws.baseball-reference.com/bullpen/Infield_fly"}, {"title": "Infield Fly", "url": "https://www.baseball-reference.com/bullpen/Infield_fly_rule"}, {"title": "Revisiting the Origin of the Infield Fly Rule", "url": "https://sabr.org/research/revisiting-origin-infield-fly-rule"}, {"title": "Infield Fly", "url": "https://www.baseball-reference.com/glossary/infield-fly/"}]}, "The search covered only two of the six terms. Infield fly and walk-off came back with useful material, and grand slams appeared only in passing. Cycle, rally cap, and seventh-inning stretch returned nothing.

**Infield fly rule:** It applies with fewer than two outs when first and second are occupied or the bases are loaded. The umpire's call makes the batter out whether or not the ball is caught, which stops the defense from setting up an easy double play. It does not cover line drives or bunts The rule applies only when there are fewer than two outs, and there is a force play at third base (which means there are runners at first and second base, or the bases are loaded). The rule does not apply on line drives nor on bunt attempts. The batter is out even if the ball drops, and the forced runners are not required to advance Because in an infield fly, the hitter is ruled out, the runners are not forced to advance.

**Walk-off:** The home team ends the game by taking the lead in the bottom of the final inning, so the visitors never get another turn at bat. The moment the winning run crosses home plate, whether by a hit, a walk, a wild pitch, or even an error, the game is officially over. A walk-off can come from a bases-loaded walk or a hit batter with the bases full, not only from a hit A bases-loaded walk, where the pitcher throws four balls to the batter, forcing a run in, is a perfectly valid (and often agonizing for the losing team) walk-off scenario.

**Grand slam:** The only mention came in a university housing page's section heading, which covered walk-off scenarios from singles to grand slams. It did not define the term, so I have no sourced definition.

**Not found:** The search returned nothing on the cycle, rally caps, or the seventh-inning stretch. A follow-up search on each of those would be needed."], "durationSeconds": 6.730776023000002, "searchCount": 1}

{"query": "Path of Exile 2 skill gems support gems tags scaling attack speed area crit ailments combos", "results": [{"tool_use_id": "srvtoolu_018ypFNZXf7Sf1KC638ukQkE", "content": [{"title": "Path of Exile 2", "url": "https://steamcommunity.com/app/2694490/discussions/0/598516531140252849"}, {"title": "www.poe2wiki.net", "url": "https://www.poe2wiki.net/wiki/Gem"}, {"title": "Spirit Gem", "url": "https://www.poe2wiki.net/wiki/Spirit_Gem"}, {"title": "deltiasgaming.com", "url": "https://deltiasgaming.com/?p=92713"}, {"title": "Additional thoughts for skill & support gem philosophy", "url": "https://www.pathofexile.com/forum/view-thread/3637820"}, {"title": "Path of Exile 2's Support Gem rule change in 0.3 is a big buff to all builds", "url": "https://www.sportskeeda.com/mmo/path-exile-2-support-gem-rule-change-0-3-poe2-third-edict"}, {"title": "Path of Exile 2: All Support Gems and Their Effects in Overview", "url": "https://mein-mmo.de/en/page/528/?term=n-w"}, {"title": "How to get more Support Gem slots for your skill in Path of Exile 2", "url": "https://sportskeeda.com/mmo/how-get-support-gem-slots-skill-path-exile-2"}, {"title": "Path of Exile 2: All Support Gems and Their Effects in Overview", "url": "https://mein-mmo.de/en/path-of-exile-2-all-support-gems-and-their-effects-in-overview,1208753"}]}, "The search returned general material on PoE 2 gems but little on your specific mechanics (attack speed, crit, ailments, combos), so those parts are unconfirmed.

**What the results cover:**
- **Gem types:** Skill gems grant active skills, and support gems modify them. The PoE 2 wiki counts 222 different skill gems, 16 different meta skill gems and 506 support gems in its older snapshot, and a newer version lists 244 skill gems and 533 support gems, so the numbers change with patches.
- **Tags drive scaling:** A user thread notes that a skill's tags decide which modifiers apply to it. Using the example of Detonate Dead, AOE support gems and skill nodes should apply to both fire and physical portion of its damage. A commenter also observes that the detonator tag does not appear to be a scaling tag. This is user opinion, not official documentation.
- **Colour and attributes:** Support gems come in red, green, and blue, tied to Strength, Dexterity, and Intelligence. A MeinMMO guide says you need sufficient intelligence to equip blue support gems.
- **Slot expansion:** Sockets can be increased with Jeweller's Orbs. Each one will add a skill slot based on how many support gem slots there already are.
- **Duplicate support gems:** The 0.3.0 "Third Edict" league removed the restriction on duplicates, so you can now use as many duplicates of a Support Gem as you want - all at the same time. Sportskeeda cites this as enabling elemental or ailment augments, such as Shock, Freeze, or Chaos, across all skills.

**Gaps:** None of the results describe attack speed, critical strike, or ailment-combo mechanics in detail. Those would need a follow-up search, ideally against the official PoE 2 wiki's support gem pages or the current patch notes, since these sources are from different patch eras."], "durationSeconds": 6.423172349999997, "searchCount": 1}

text:

{"query": "game feel hit stop hitlag telegraph animation canceling action RPG combat feel explained", "results": [{"tool_use_id": "srvtoolu_01YM6g37pFkBVuPqpuhfXkw7", "content": [{"title": "ken.ieice.org", "url": "https://ken.ieice.org/ken/paper/20230315OCSt/eng/"}, {"title": "dev notesgame feelcombat", "url": "https://gamer-ai-nexgen.duckdns.org/blog/anatomy-of-a-good-game-punch"}, {"title": "RPG Combat Feel Prototype", "url": "https://macionik.itch.io/rpg-battle"}, {"title": "Monster Hunter Wilds", "url": "https://steamcommunity.com/app/2246340/discussions/0/4630357016599074272"}, {"title": "faculty.washington.edu", "url": "https://faculty.washington.edu/zkwen/articles/lin22features.pdf"}, {"title": "전투 시스템 기획의 정석 액션 어드벤", "url": "https://www.inflearn.com/en/course/전투-시스템-기획의-정석-액션-어드벤?cid=339752"}, {"title": "Monster Hunter Wilds", "url": "https://steamcommunity.com/app/2246340/discussions/0/4633737175312187465"}, {"title": "【Unity】Fixing "My Attacks Don't Feel Like They Hit": A Game Feel Primer with Hit Stop, Flash, Shake, and Sound", "url": "https://uhiyama-lab.com/en/notes/unity/unity-game-feel-hit-feedback/"}, {"title": "inflearn logo", "url": "https://www.inflearn.com/en/course/전투-시스템-기획의-정석-액션-어드벤"}]}, "The search covered hit stop and game feel well, but returned nothing on telegraphs or animation canceling, so those need a separate search.

**Hit stop / hitlag**
- A Japanese study on 3D action games tested hit stop durations. It found the best pause was roughly 0.1 to 0.2 seconds, and slow-motion worked best at about 0.2 to 0.4 seconds. The optimum duration for Hit-Stop effects was approx. 0.1 to 0.2 seconds, and the optimum duration for slow-motion effects was slightly longer, approx. 0.2 to 0.4 seconds.
- A research paper on impact feel found that hit stop, sound coherence, and camera control may strongly influence players' impact feel. It also said that weak design in any one of these three can hurt the result.
- Player reception is mixed. In Monster Hunter Wilds discussions, some players argued that hitstop is essential for balancing attacks and conveying resistance, while others said it makes the game look like it stutters. These are forum comments, not systematic data.

**Game feel basics**
- A Unity-focused guide describes the common problem of attacks feeling like they hit a pillow. It argues that effects such as hit flash, particles, sound, camera shake, and hit stop deliver the fact "you hit it" to the player's eyes and ears.
- The term "game feel" comes from Swink's book, where it describes real time control of virtual objects in a simulated space, with interactions emphasized by polish.

**Not covered by these results**
- Telegraph animations and animation canceling in action RPGs. A follow-up search on those terms would be needed."], "durationSeconds": 6.316108071000002, "searchCount": 1}

{"query": "Diablo IV Barbarian skills basic core ultimate fury generator spender key passive Bash Hammer of the Ancients mechanics", "results": [{"tool_use_id": "srvtoolu_01SeRKF81X3sQBmrU6m8vofL", "content": [{"title": "Diablo IV: Best Barbarian Leveling Build For Season 1", "url": "https://gameluster.com/?p=92376"}, {"title": "Diablo IV: Best Barbarian Leveling Build For Season 1", "url": "https://gameluster.com/diablo-iv-best-barbarian-leveling-build-for-season-1/"}, {"title": "All NewsDiablo IV", "url": "https://maxroll.gg/d4/build-guides/hammer-of-the-ancients-barbarian-leveling-guide"}, {"title": "diablo 4 barbarian build hammer barbarian build guide", "url": "https://fextralife.com/diablo-4-barbarian-build-hammer-barbarian-build-guide/"}, {"title": "barbarian hota barbarian", "url": "https://mobalytics.gg/diablo-4/builds/barbarian-hota-barbarian"}, {"title": "Barbarian Core Skills", "url": "https://www.purediablo.com/diablo4/Barbarian_Core_Skills"}, {"title": "What can you do as a free member?", "url": "https://game8.co/games/Diablo-4/archives/414025"}, {"title": "The Devil's Anvil", "url": "https://diablowiki.net/The_Devil%27s_Anvil"}, {"title": "fextralife.com", "url": "https://diablo4.wiki.fextralife.com/Barbarian+Skills"}]}, "Here's what the search turned up. The sources come from different patches and seasons, and they don't fully agree, so check the current game version before relying on specific numbers.

**Fury economy:** Barbarian Fury Skills spend the Fury that Basic Skills generate, and which Fury skills you can use depends on your weapon type. One source lists Rend, Hammer of the Ancients, Double Swing, Upheaval, and Whirlwind as the five Fury spenders (fextralife). Ultimates have long cooldowns, and Wrath of the Berserker generates Fury and rewards spending it (fextralife).

**Hammer of the Ancients:** It is a Fury spender that needs a Two-Handed Bludgeoning weapon (purediablo). Its cost is listed as 35 Fury in one source (purediablo) and 20 in another (fextralife), so this figure varies by version. Casting it at full Fury is the main damage pattern. Furious Hammer of the Ancients scales with the Fury you have when you cast it (game8). Maxroll describes it as the build's main damage dealer, becoming a larger shockwave after the Ancestral Force aspect (maxroll).

**Generators and Bash:** Leap is paired with Bash for efficient Fury generation, and Bash pairs well with a Two-Handed Mace (fextralife). Enhanced Frenzy, Rallying Cry, and Power Leap are cited as Fury sources in a leveling guide (gameluster). I found no detailed Bash numbers in these results.

**Passives:** Walking Arsenal gives extra damage when using specific weapon types and is used for weapon swapping (gameluster). Endless Fury makes Basic Skills generate more Fury with Two-Handed weapons (purediablo).

**Gaps:** The results don't cover current-season Bash values or the latest Hammer of the Ancients cost, and they don't cover full Ultimate lists, since one source leaves a placeholder for the fourth one."], "durationSeconds": 7.812743649, "searchCount": 1}

It covered most of your terms, but not all of them.

- **Hit for the cycle:** A batter who gets a single, double, triple, and home run in the same game. One glossary also calls it "hitting the cycle" When a batter hits a single, double, triple, and home run in the same game. This is also commonly referred to as "hitting for the cycle".
- **Squeeze play:** A bunt meant to drive in a runner from third. One fan guide describes it as A bunt designed to bring a runner home from third base.
- **Rundown:** A play where a baserunner is caught between bases. It's also called a "pickle." Pickle — A run-down. When a base runner gets caught between bases by the fielders.
- **Pickoff:** The results didn't define the pickoff play itself. The closest entries are MLB's slang list, which says a runner who is picked off is caught napping, and a note that "pick" is a shortened version of "pick-off."
- **Rally cap:** Not covered in any of the results.
- **Seventh-inning stretch origin:** Not covered in any of the results. Searching for it separately would be needed."], "durationSeconds": 6.364746107000006, "searchCount": 1}

id: note:13:Research 1: Baseball batting (for BAT ARPG skills)
name: Research 1: Baseball batting (for BAT ARPG skills)
text:
Research 1: Baseball batting (for BAT ARPG skills)
SOURCED (FanGraphs/Statcast, SABR): sweet spot = ~2in zone centred ~6in from barrel end; MLB bat speed there 65-85 mph. Statcast "barrel" = exit velo >=98 mph with launch angle ~26-30deg (widens as EV rises). Optimal HR launch angle ~20-30deg; line drives 10-25deg; ground balls <10; pop-ups >50. Exit velo depends on bat speed + pitch speed + contact quality (SABR: swing path, kinetic sequencing, bat speed matter most). Perfect contact vs. jammed/topped/foul-tip are the quality tiers.
COMMON KNOWLEDGE (unsourced): swing phases = stance -> load (weight back, hands back) -> stride -> trigger/rotation (hips then torso then arms then bat: kinetic chain) -> contact -> extension -> follow-through. Timing windows: early = pull/foul, late = opposite field. Pull/center/opposite field. Check swing = bat stopped mid-swing; umpire judges if barrel crossed front of plate. Bunt = square up, deaden ball with bat held out: sacrifice (move runner), squeeze (suicide/safety; runner on 3rd scores), drag/push bunt for hit. Switch hitter bats L vs R to face pitcher's opposite hand. Bat flip = showy toss after big hit; home-run trot = slow circuit of bases, tipping cap, pointing to sky; unwritten-rule culture/showboating. Grand slam = HR with bases loaded (4 runs). Fouls: foul tip, foul ball counts as strike until 2 strikes. Intentional walk, hit by pitch. Terms: whiff, dinger, moonshot, ducksnort, frozen rope, can of corn, golden sombrero (4K), rally cap.
FEEL notes: perfect-timing = hit-stop + crack sound + camera punch; ball trajectory arcs (launch angle) readable as projectile arcs; sweet-spot = precision/timing mechanic scalable to crit.
Links: BRIEF.md

name: Research 2: Pitching, fielding, baserunning
text:
Research 2: Pitching, fielding, baserunning
PITCHES (Magnus effect: spin axis => force direction; sources comsol, snexplores, WashU): four-seam fastball = backspin lift, 90-100 mph, 'rises' (drops less than gravity). Curveball = topspin, extra ~30cm drop, 70-80 mph, 12-6 or 11-5 break. Slider = sidespin/gyro, late sharp lateral break, 82-90 mph; sweeper = slider w/ big horizontal sweep (~80 mph). Changeup = fastball arm speed, 8-12 mph slower, fade/tail & drop; splitter = ball jammed between fingers, low spin, late tumbling drop, fast for offspeed. Knuckleball = near-zero spin, vortex shedding => erratic flutter, 60-80 mph, hard for catcher too. Screwball = reverse curve (breaks opposite lateral direction), rare/legendary (Mike Marshall, Fernando Valenzuela, Carl Hubbell). Eephus = extreme-lob 'junk' pitch, 53-60 mph (sourced MLB), high arc, batter must supply power; works on timing disruption. Cutter, sinker also. Principle: velocity differential + deception, tunneling.
FIELDING (common knowledge): double play (6-4-3 shortstop->2nd->1st; around-the-horn 5-4-3; force at 2nd), diving catch/web gem, shoestring catch, relay/cutoff throw (outfielder -> cutoff man -> plate), tag play at plate/blocking, rundown/'pickle' (runner trapped between bases, throw & chase), pickoff (pitcher/catcher throws to base to catch leaning runner; 'caught napping'; balk if fake illegal), force vs tag, infield fly, catcher's pop-time, framing, cannon arm. 
BASERUNNING: steal (jump, lead-off, slide; catcher pop time), slides (head-first, hook, pop-up, feet-first), tag up (runner must retouch base after fly caught, then advance; sac fly), hit-and-run, squeeze, dropped third strike, lead-off. Sources: comsol.com physics blog, texasleaguers magnus, snexplores, MLB slow pitches, mlb glossary.
Links: BRIEF.md

name: Research 3: Baseball rules, situations, culture
text:
Research 3: Baseball rules, situations, culture
SOURCED: Infield fly = <2 outs, runners on 1st&2nd or loaded, fair fly catchable by infielder w/ ordinary effort; batter out whether or not caught; no line drives/bunts; prevents trap double play (baseball-reference, Wikipedia). Walk-off = home team takes lead in bottom of final inning, game ends instant winning run scores (even bases-loaded walk/HBP). Cycle = single+double+triple+HR in one game. Rundown = 'pickle'. Squeeze = bunt to score runner from 3rd. 
COMMON KNOWLEDGE: 3 strikes = out (K; backwards K = called third strike), 4 balls = walk (BB), 3 outs per half inning, 9 innings, 6 (little league) -- 3 strikes, ball 4; strike zone; hit by pitch. Grand slam = HR w/ bases loaded. Bases loaded = force at every base, max pressure. Rally cap = fans wear cap inside-out/backwards to spark comeback. Seventh-inning stretch: fans stand & sing 'Take Me Out to the Ball Game' before bottom of 7th. Rally monkey, 'Casey at the Bat' (mighty Casey strikes out), 'Field of Dreams'. Umpire calls: ball/strike, safe/out, fair/foul, balk, checked swing appeal, ejection ('you're outta here'), strike-em-out-throw-em-out, instant replay. Little league: 'everyone bats', mercy rule, orange slices, snack bar, sunflower seeds, dugout chants ('hey batter batter swing!'), tee-ball, parents in lawn chairs, dusk under lights, coach's pep talk, Dixie cups of Gatorade, dirt-covered uniforms, 'ump' with big mask. Hit streak, no-hitter/perfect game, golden sombrero, hat trick, called shot (Babe Ruth), curse of the Bambino. Lineup order: leadoff, cleanup (4th, power hitter), pinch hitter, closer, bullpen, walk-up song, stadium organ.

name: Research 4: ARPG skill design (POE2, D4, game feel)
text:
Research 4: ARPG skill design (POE2, D4, game feel)
POE2 (poe2wiki, maxroll, sportskeeda): skill gems = active skills with TAGS (Attack, Melee, Strike, Slam, AoE, Physical, Fire, Projectile, Duration, Warcry, Travel...) that decide which modifiers apply; support gems (red/Str, green/Dex, blue/Int) modify linked skill via sockets; since 0.3 duplicate supports allowed. Meta gems trigger other skills; Spirit reserved for persistent buffs/minions. Mace skills (Warrior): Heavy Stun system - stun buildup, enemies 'Primed' at 60% (magic) / 70% (rare) / 80% (unique) buildup; Boneshatter strike Heavy Stuns primed enemies and makes a shockwave; Leap Slam primes; Mace Strike primes; Earthquake (slam w/ aftershock) used on stunned bosses; Seismic Cry doubles next slam vs Heavy Stunned -> COMBO = prime then pay-off. Other POE2 knowledge (common): Combo counters on skills, Culling Strike executes low-HP, ailments: ignite/shock/freeze/chill/bleed/poison, crit chance/multiplier, attack speed scales both skill rate & dps, area of effect radius, cooldown + charges, Rage, Armour/Evasion, dodge roll baseline.
D4 (purediablo, fextralife, maxroll): Barbarian Basic skills GENERATE Fury (Bash, Frenzy, Flay, Lunging Strike); Core/Fury skills SPEND (Hammer of the Ancients 20-35 Fury, Whirlwind channel, Rend, Upheaval, Double Swing); Defensive (Ground Stomp, Rallying Cry, Iron Skin), Brawling, Weapon Mastery, Ultimates (long cooldown e.g. Wrath of the Berserker, Call of the Ancients, Iron Maelstrom), Key Passives. Generator/spender loop; spend at full resource for bonus (Furious HotA); Walking Arsenal = weapon swap.
GAME FEEL (Japanese study ken.ieice, Unity game-feel primer): hit-stop optimum ~0.1-0.2s, slow-mo ~0.2-0.4s; impact feel = hit stop + sound coherence + camera control (weak in any one hurts); hit flash, particles, screenshake, knockback, squash/stretch. Telegraphs: ground decals/windup poses with clear shape & colour; animation cancel (dodge/skill cancels recovery frames), anticipation->strike->follow-through; readable VFX silhouettes; colour-coded elements; audio pitch tied to hit power; big finisher gets longer stop.

id: note:17:Research 5: It Takes Two - everyday themes to mech
name: Research 5: It Takes Two - everyday themes to mechanics
text:
Research 5: It Takes Two - everyday themes to mechanics
Sources: exitlag, hone.gg chapter guides. Pattern: each chapter = one household theme turned into a paired ability set + a distinct level gimmick; abilities used together, sometimes whole chapter, sometimes one section. The Shed: hammer (smash, swing from nails) + throwable nails (pin objects, swing points, platforms); tools as terrain. The Tree: sap gun (goop on enemies/objects) + match/flame gun detonates sap (combo = status then detonator; squirrels war). Rose's Room: genre-shifting, toy-box minigames. Cuckoo Clock: time modify/rewind + clones of self to teleport to; clock gears as platforms. Snow Globe: magnets (attract/repel, pairing polarity), ice rink. Garden: water + plant growth + grappling hook onto plants, vacuum/wasp enemies. Attic/Toy: music, flight. Finale/Kaleidoscope. General lessons: (1) giant-scale scenery as arena (tools, nails, clocks), (2) the object IS the mechanic (hammer=hammer), (3) two-part combo abilities (apply + detonate), (4) each area has a fresh ability so novelty every chapter, (5) comedy/cartoon physics boss fights (vacuum cleaner, Dr Hakim book). For our game: sprinklers, wind-up toys, lawn gnomes, vacuums as enemies/hazards; ballfield dusk: dugout, scoreboard, backstop, sprinklers, pitching machine, bases, chalk lines, snack bar.
Links: BRIEF.md
